title: Fix a claim status filter
tagline: The open-claims filter returns the wrong rows. Reproduce the bug, explain the comparison, and fix it.
intro: Thanks for making the time. This round is a bug fix in a small Java filter. The open-claims queue is returning closed claims. You have the broken class and a failing test. Explain the root cause before changing the comparison.
reproductionNote: Support ticket FILTER-12: "The open-claims screen shows closed claims and hides open ones. Repro: filter [C1 OPEN, C2 CLOSED, C3 OPEN]; the result contains C2 instead of C1 and C3." Run OpenClaimsFilterTest in the hidden suite.

diagnosis.prompt: Explain the root cause in your own words: why does the filter return the wrong status, and what comparison should it use?
diagnosis.strongAnswer: The condition is inverted: !claim.status().equals("OPEN") keeps every non-open claim and drops open ones, so the comparison is wrong. Remove the negation and keep only claims whose status equals OPEN.

clarifyingQuestions.question: What does the support ticket say is wrong?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: The ticket says closed claims appear and open claims disappear. Reproduce it with a mixed list before editing.
clarifyingQuestions.coach: Ask for the reported behaviour and reproduce it first.

clarifyingQuestions.question: Should I rewrite the whole filter or change one line?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: Change only the status comparison. Keep the loop, the return type, and the method signature.
clarifyingQuestions.coach: Ask how wide the fix should be before editing.

clarifyingQuestions.question: What follow-up change is coming?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: The follow-up adds REOPENED claims to the same open queue, so keep the comparison easy to extend.
clarifyingQuestions.coach: Ask about the follow-up so the fix leaves room for it.

clarifyingFallback: Assume the filter is a pure in-memory method, the input list is non-null, and order must be preserved. Reproduce the failure before editing.
problemStatement:
### Context

ClaimFilter builds the open-claims queue for the intake dashboard. A support ticket says closed claims appear in the queue and open claims are missing.

### Your task

Read the broken class, reproduce the failure, identify the root cause, and fix the filter.

### Rules

- openOnly returns only claims whose status is exactly "OPEN".
- Keep the order of the input list.
- Do not modify the input list.
- Empty input returns an empty list.
- Change only the comparison; keep the method signature and the loop shape.

### Reproduction

The ticket and the failing test are above the editor. Explain the root cause before editing.

hiddenTests.name: open claims filter keeps only OPEN
all closed claims return an empty list
input order is preserved
an empty list returns an empty list

changeRequest.prompt: Include reopened claims in the open queue.
changeRequest.statement:
### Change request

Reopened claims should appear in the same queue.

- openOnly returns claims whose status is exactly "OPEN" or exactly "REOPENED".
- Preserve input order, leave the input list unchanged, and return an empty list for empty input.
- CLOSED and any other status stay out.

hiddenTests.name: reopened claims join the open queue
closed and other statuses stay out of the queue
open-only input still works after the change

probes.text: Which claim does the current condition keep, and which claim should it keep?
State the root cause in one sentence before you edit the comparison.

fallbackProbe: What is the smallest change that makes the failing test pass without touching the loop?

phasePrompts.brief: Read the ticket and the class, then ask me any questions you have. Reproduce the failure before editing.
phasePrompts.implement: The timer is running. Say which condition is wrong, then make the smallest comparison change.
phasePrompts.test: Run the tests. Confirm the regression test now passes for the reason you predicted.
phasePrompts.change: Here is the change request. Extend the status check without disturbing the base behaviour.
phasePrompts.debrief: Time is up. Let us review the diagnosis, the fix, the tests, and the rubric.

hints: Read the if condition as English: which statuses pass it right now?
The negation flips the test. Remove it and compare directly with OPEN.
Change only the comparison: if (claim.status().equals("OPEN")). Keep the loop and the return type.

rubric.criterion: The status filter passes the hidden suite
rubric.strongAnswer: Only OPEN claims are returned, order is preserved, and empty or all-closed input returns an empty list.

rubric.criterion: The reopened-claims change passes the hidden suite
rubric.strongAnswer: OPEN and REOPENED claims are included while CLOSED claims stay out.
Names the negated status test, explains why it keeps closed claims, and states the corrected comparison.
Asked what the ticket reports, how wide the fix should be, and what the follow-up adds.
Found the inverted comparison with no hints, or after one hint following a genuine attempt.
